proof_summary: For Lemoine’s conjecture, swap the two primes in the assumed representation for all values above the cutoff, and check the finitely many smaller odd values explicitly. For twin primes, if there were only finitely many, injectivity of the prime-enumerating map would make the admissible primes finite; taking their odd product \(P\) and applying the hypothesis to \(21P=2n+1\) yields primes \(p,q\) with \(p\mid P\), hence \(p\mid q\) and \(1<p<q\), contradicting the primality of \(q\).
